name: One Pot Caribbean Jerk Chicken and Rice
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.5 lb (2911 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rub the chicken thighs with the jerk seasoning, dried thyme, paprika, cajun seasoning, salt and black pepper. Let them sit at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge if you have the time.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy oven-safe pot over medium-high and sear the thighs in batches until the seasoning darkens and sticks. Set them aside; they finish later.
Cook the diced onion in the same pot for 4 minutes, then add the garlic, the minced jalapeno and the bay leaves and cook one more minute.
Stir in the rice and the drained kidney beans and toast for two minutes so the grains take on the jerk fond off the bottom.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken broth, scrape the pot clean, and bring it to a boil. Lay the chicken back on top with any juices.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest burner setting, or in a 350F oven, for 25 to 30 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reads 165F. Rest it covered another 10 minutes off the heat.
Pull the bay leaves, chop the chicken, fold everything together in your mixing pot, and finish with the sliced green onions.

name: One-Pot Turkey Mexican Pasta
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 44 oz dry (1244 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 5 oz (145 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in your largest pot and brown the ground turkey hard, breaking it into crumbles and letting it stick a little before you scrape it up.
Add the diced onion and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, chili powder, ground cumin, dried oregano, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper for one minute.
Pour in the salsa and the chicken broth, scraping the bottom of the pot clean, and bring it to a hard boil.
Stir in the dry pasta shells, making sure they are submerged, then drop to a simmer and cook uncovered 12 to 14 minutes.
Stir every few minutes so the shells do not weld to the bottom. This is the one part of a one-pot pasta that actually demands attention.
When the pasta is tender and the sauce has thickened around it, kill the heat and let the pot stand 5 minutes.
Stir in the light sour cream and the shredded cheddar off the heat so they melt smoothly instead of breaking.

name: One-Pot Ground Turkey Stroganoff
ingredients: Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 32.5 oz dry (919 g)
1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 3.5 oz (99 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Melt the butter in your big pot and cook the diced onion 3 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 more.
Add the ground turkey and brown it, breaking it up, until it reads 165 F with no pink. Season with the thyme, salt, and pepper.
Add the mushrooms and cook 6 to 8 minutes until they release their water and it cooks off.
Pour in the chicken broth and Worcestershire, bring to a boil, and stir in the egg noodles. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring so nothing sticks, until the noodles are just tender.
Kill the heat. Stir in the dijon, sour cream, and cream cheese until the sauce is smooth.
Fold in the thawed spinach until warmed through, then taste for salt.

name: One-Skillet Ground Turkey Thai Curry with Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground turkey in your biggest deep skillet or pot over medium-high, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reads 165 F.
Add the grated ginger, turmeric, paprika, and cinnamon and stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the sliced carrots, then add the dry rice and stir to coat it in the spices.
Pour in the coconut milk, chicken broth, soy sauce, and fish sauce. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low about 15 minutes.
Scatter the chopped zucchini on top, cover again, and cook 5 to 8 more minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest 5 minutes off heat, then fold in the fresh basil and taste for salt and pepper.

name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Broccoli
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 32.5 oz dry (919 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (1 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Bring a large pot of well salted water to a boil. Salting the water is your only chance to season the pasta itself.
Boil the pasta shells, and add the broccoli florets to the same pot for the last few minutes so they cook in the pasta water.
Reserve a couple of mugs of that starchy water before draining, then drain the pasta and broccoli together.
While the pasta cooks, brown the hot Italian sausage in crumbles in a wide skillet until it takes on real color.
Add the butter and the minced garlic to the sausage along with the red pepper flakes and black pepper, and cook just until fragrant.
Return the drained pasta and broccoli to your big pot, pour the sausage and garlic butter over it, and add the parmesan.
Splash in the reserved pasta water a little at a time and toss hard. The starch and the cheese emulsify into a light sauce that coats everything.

name: Oven Baked Country-Style Pork Chops with Potatoes
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 2.25 tbsp (35 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F and line two large sheet pans.
Whisk the Worcestershire, ketchup, soy sauce, brown sugar, olive oil, minced garlic and apple cider vinegar together into a glossy glaze.
Cut the potatoes into even wedges, toss them with about a third of the glaze plus salt and pepper, and spread them in a single layer on the pans.
Roast the potatoes alone first so they get a head start and start to brown at the edges.
Season the pork chops, nestle them among the potatoes, and brush them generously with the remaining glaze.
Return the pans to the oven and bake until the chops hit 145F inside and the glaze has gone sticky.
Rest the chops five minutes, then slice them off the bone and combine everything in your big pot with the pan juices.

name: Oyakodon (Japanese Chicken and Egg Rice Bowls)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.25 lb (1984 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 7 cups dry with water per your usual method.
In your big pot, combine the chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken thighs cut into bite-size pieces and most of the green onions. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken reads 165 F.
Beat the eggs lightly, just until streaky, not uniform.
Pour the eggs evenly over the simmering chicken, cover, and cook 2 to 3 minutes. For meal prep that reheats safely, cook the eggs fully set, not runny.
Spoon the chicken and egg mixture with plenty of broth over rice in each container and top with the remaining green onions.

name: Pakistani Beef Kofta Curry
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Mix the ground beef with a small amount of finely grated onion, minced jalapeno, chopped cilantro, the flour, and the ground cumin, coriander, chili powder, and salt. Knead it until it is smooth and slightly sticky.
Roll the mixture into even meatballs and set them on a tray in the fridge while you build the gravy.
Slice the rest of the onions thin and fry them in the vegetable oil over medium heat, patiently, until they are deep golden brown. This step is the entire dish, so do not rush it.
Add the minced garlic and the turmeric and cook 1 minute, then take the pot off the heat for a moment.
Whisk the Greek yogurt smooth and stir it in off the heat so it does not split, then return the pot to low and cook until the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Lower the koftas into the gravy in a single layer, add a cup or so of water, cover, and simmer 25 to 30 minutes. Shake the pot instead of stirring so the meatballs hold together.
Finish with garam masala and the remaining cilantro, and cook the rice separately.

name: Pakistani Chapli Kebab Rice Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.5 tbsp (3 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Crush the whole coriander seeds coarsely, then mix them with the ground cumin, red pepper flakes, chili powder, black pepper, and salt.
Combine the ground beef with the finely chopped red onion, green onions, minced jalapeno, garlic, ginger, cilantro, eggs, all-purpose flour, pomegranate molasses, and the spice mix.
Fold in the drained diced tomatoes last and gently, so they stay in pieces instead of turning the mixture to slurry.
Chill the mixture for thirty minutes, which makes it far easier to shape.
Form wide, flat, thin patties, brush the sheet pans and the tops with the vegetable oil, and lay them out without touching.
Bake at 425 degrees, flipping once, until browned and crisp at the edges and cooked through.
Cook the rice according to the package while the kebabs bake.

name: Panang Chicken Curry
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 2.5 lb (1135 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Soak the dried chiles in hot water for 20 minutes. Drain them and blend with the peanuts, lemongrass paste, ginger, garlic, ground coriander, salt and a splash of the soaking water into a thick, coarse paste.

Spoon the thick cream off the top of the unshaken coconut milk cans into your largest pot, reserving the thin liquid. Cook it with the vegetable oil over medium-high for 3 to 5 minutes until the oil splits out.
Add your panang paste and the diced onion and fry it in that oil for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring hard, until it darkens a shade and smells nutty and sharp at the same time.
Add the chicken thighs cut into strips and turn them in the paste for 3 minutes, then pour in the reserved coconut liquid and the chicken broth.
Simmer uncovered 20 to 25 minutes, letting the sauce reduce until it is genuinely thick. Panang is supposed to cling, not pool, so give it the time.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar, add the green beans, and cook 4 minutes until they are tender but still have snap.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fresh basil. Cook the rice separately, steam it covered 10 minutes, and fold it in or bed the curry on top of it.

name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Cajun Dirty Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice in the chicken broth (3.5 cups dry rice in about half the broth), then set aside. Slightly firm is perfect since it cooks again.
Brown the chorizo in your big pot over medium-high, breaking it up, until it renders and crisps in spots.
Add the diced onion, red bell pepper, and garlic and cook 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the thyme and a spoon of the cajun seasoning.
Fold in the cooked rice and a splash of remaining broth, scraping the bottom, until every grain turns the color dirty rice is named for. Finish with green onions.
Pat the chops dry, season hard with the rest of the cajun seasoning, salt, and pepper, and sear in olive oil 3 to 4 minutes per side until they reach 145 F.
Rest the chops 5 minutes, slice, and serve over the dirty rice.

name: Parmesan Garlic Sheet-Pan Chicken Thighs and Potatoes
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3 lb (1400 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Cut the potatoes into bite-size chunks, toss them with most of the olive oil, salt, black pepper and paprika, and spread them across two large sheet pans in a single layer.
Roast the potatoes alone for 20 minutes, until the edges are starting to color. They need the head start; the chicken does not.
While they roast, stir together the melted butter, mayonnaise, minced garlic, grated parmesan, lemon juice and italian seasoning into a thick paste.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and coat every piece in the parmesan garlic mixture, front and back.
Pull the pans, push the potatoes to the edges, and nestle the coated thighs into the middle with the green beans scattered around them.
Roast another 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken reads 165F, the coating is browned and blistered in spots, and the potatoes are crisp underneath.
Chop the chicken into pieces, scrape everything into your mixing pot with the pan drippings, and toss so the garlic butter coats the potatoes and beans too.

name: Pasta alla Norcina Creamy Sausage Pasta
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne in well salted water to just under al dente, since it will finish in the sauce. Save a couple cups of the pasta water before draining.
Squeeze the sausage out of its casings and break it into rough crumbles.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and cook the sausage over medium-high heat until browned in spots, not just gray.
Add the finely diced yellow onion and cook until soft and translucent.
Pour in the chicken broth, scrape the bottom of the pot clean, and let it reduce by about half.
Lower the heat, stir in the heavy cream, and simmer gently until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Do not let it boil hard or it will separate.
Add the drained penne and the parmesan, toss until every piece is coated, loosen with pasta water if needed, and season with salt and plenty of black pepper.

name: Pastel de Choclo (Chilean Beef and Corn Casserole)
ingredients: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 3 cans (1323 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the diced yellow onions slowly until soft and sweet, which is the base of the pino.
Add the garlic, ground cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper and cook for a minute.
Add the ground beef, break it up, and cook until browned, then sprinkle in the all-purpose flour and stir it through.
Pour in the chicken broth and simmer until the filling is thick and saucy rather than wet, then fold in the olives and golden raisins.
For the corn layer, blend the sweet corn with the milk and fresh basil until mostly smooth, then cook it in a pot with the butter and grits, stirring, until it thickens to a soft porridge.
Spread the beef filling in a large baking dish, arrange the hard boiled eggs over it, and spread the corn mixture across the top.
Sprinkle the sugar over the corn layer and bake at 400 degrees until the top is set and browned in patches.

name: Pastitsio (Greek Beef Pasta Bake)
ingredients: Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7.5 oz (210 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the spaghetti two minutes short of package time, drain, and toss with a little of the melted butter and about a third of the feta.

Make the meat sauce: brown the beef with the red onion and garlic in olive oil, then add diced tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, sugar, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Simmer 20 minutes until thick, then pull the bay leaves.

Make the bechamel: melt the butter in your big pot, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk gradually. Simmer, whisking, until it coats a spoon. Off heat, whisk in the nutmeg and most of the parmesan.
Temper the beaten eggs into the warm bechamel a ladle at a time, whisking constantly so they enrich instead of scramble.
Layer in a deep greased 9x13: pasta, all the meat sauce, then the bechamel poured over the top. Sprinkle with the remaining parmesan and feta.
Bake at 350 F for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden, then rest at least 20 minutes so it slices clean.

name: Pepper Steak with Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Freeze the steak for about 30 minutes so it firms up, then slice it thin against the grain. Toss the slices with a spoonful of the cornstarch and a splash of the soy sauce and let them sit while you prep everything else.
Start the rice.

Whisk the rest of the soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, sesame oil, and remaining cornstarch together with a little water. Having the sauce ready in a cup before you start is the whole secret to stir frying, because once the pan is hot there is no time to measure anything.
Get a large skillet very hot with the vegetable oil and sear the beef in batches, about 90 seconds a side. Pull it out while it is still slightly underdone. It will finish in the sauce.
Add the sliced peppers, onion, and jalapeno to the same pan and cook hard for 3 to 4 minutes. You want them blistered at the edges and still crisp in the middle, not soft.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then pour in the sauce and let it bubble and thicken.
Return the beef and any juices, toss everything together for a minute, and season with paprika, salt, and plenty of black pepper.

name: Peri Peri Chicken and Rice
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4 lb (1820 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Build the peri peri base: stir the hot sauce together with the cajun seasoning, ground coriander, ground turmeric, dried oregano, minced garlic, salt and black pepper. Toss the chicken thighs in about two thirds of it and let them sit while the oven heats to 375F.

Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or deep roasting pan over medium-high and sear the marinated thighs in batches until they are browned on both sides. They will not be cooked through yet. Set them aside.
Cook the diced onion and green bell pepper in the same pot for 5 minutes, scraping up the fond as they release their water.
Stir in the dry rice and the remaining peri peri base and toast for two minutes so every grain picks up color.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring it to a boil, then lay the chicken back on top with any juices from the plate.
Cover tightly and bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reads 165F. Let it sit covered off the heat for 10 minutes before you touch it.
Chop the chicken, fold everything together in your mixing pot, and finish with the sliced green onions and chopped cilantro.

name: Persian Fesenjan Chicken (Walnut-Pomegranate Stew) Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3 lb (1400 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 3.75 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Toast the walnuts in your dry pot over medium heat, stirring, 5 minutes until fragrant. Cool slightly, then grind them fine in a food processor.
Cook the diced onion in the olive oil until golden, then stir in the turmeric and cinnamon for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken thighs cut into chunks and stir 2 to 3 minutes to coat.
Add the ground walnuts and enough water to make a loose sauce, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook low for 30 minutes, stirring so the walnuts do not stick.
Stir in the pomegranate molasses, sugar, salt, and pepper and simmer uncovered 15 to 20 more minutes until the stew is thick and dark and the chicken reads 165 F.
Taste and balance: more molasses for tart, a pinch more sugar for sweet. Serve over the rice.

name: Persian Kabob Koobideh Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 3.75 cups dry with water per your usual method. Melt the butter into the hot rice and fluff.
Grate the onions on a box grater and squeeze the pulp firmly to remove most of the juice. Wet meat falls apart, so squeeze like you mean it.
Knead the beef with the squeezed onion, garlic, paprika, turmeric, salt, and pepper for a good 3 to 4 minutes until it turns sticky and pasty. That texture is what holds koobideh together.
Shape into long flat logs, about one wide log per serving, and press a light zigzag pattern in with your fingers, kabob-house style.
Broil on high on a foil-lined pan 4 to 5 minutes per side, or grill over hot coals, until browned outside with no pink in the middle.
Rest 5 minutes, then serve over the buttered rice with any pan juices poured back on top.

name: Persian Turkey Loobia Polo (Green Bean Rice)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then soak it in salted water for 30 minutes while you cook everything else. This is the step that makes the grains separate instead of clump.
Dice the onion and cook it in the olive oil over medium heat until golden, about 10 minutes, then add the garlic and turmeric for one minute.
Add the ground turkey and brown it, breaking it up as it goes, until it is cooked through to 165F. Stir in the tomato paste, cinnamon, salt, and pepper and cook two minutes more.
Add the green beans, a splash of water, and the lemon juice, then cover and cook 10 minutes until the beans are tender and the pan is barely wet.
Parboil the drained rice in a big pot of boiling salted water for 6 to 8 minutes, until the grains are soft outside and still firm in the middle, then drain.

Film the bottom of a heavy pot with the vegetable oil, layer in the rice and the turkey and bean mixture in alternating scoops, poke a few steam holes through with a spoon handle, cover with a towel-wrapped lid, and steam on low for 40 minutes.
Scoop the whole thing into your weighed pot, crust and all, and fold gently so every serving gets rice and meat both.

name: Peruvian Pollo Saltado
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 4.25 lb (1905 g)
Aji Amarillo Paste (Goya (Yellow Hot Pepper Paste)): 2.25 oz (67 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the chicken breast into thick strips and marinate it with the soy sauce, ground cumin, dried oregano, black pepper, aji amarillo paste and white vinegar for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat. Bake the frozen fries on a sheet pan at 425F until they are genuinely crisp, not just hot. Keep them separate for now.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or wok as hot as your burner goes and sear the chicken in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per batch, until browned. Do not crowd it. Set the chicken aside.
Add the red onion cut into thick wedges, plus the red and green bell pepper strips, and stir fry hard for 2 to 3 minutes. They should stay crunchy; wilted onion is the mark of a saltado gone wrong.
Add the garlic and grated ginger for 30 seconds, then the drained diced tomatoes, and toss for another minute.
Return the chicken with all the marinade, let it bubble and reduce for 2 minutes, and taste for salt and vinegar.
Fold the crisp fries and the chopped cilantro in at the very last second, then combine with the rice in your mixing pot.

name: Peruvian Sheet-Pan Chicken Thighs with Green Sauce
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.75 lb (2100 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Whisk the olive oil, white vinegar, lemon juice, ground cumin, paprika, garlic powder, dried oregano, salt and black pepper into a marinade. Add the chicken thighs, turn them until every piece is coated, and refrigerate overnight if you can spare the time, or at least four hours if you cannot.
Heat the oven to 425F. Spread the sliced yellow onion across a large sheet pan and lay the marinated thighs on top so the onion catches everything that drips.
Roast 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken reads 165F and the edges have gone dark and a little sticky. Do not crowd the pan; use two if you need to.
While it roasts, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes.

Make the aji verde: blend the cilantro, jalapeno, garlic, mayonnaise and lime juice with a pinch of salt until it is completely smooth and bright green. Taste it and add more chile if you want it to bite back.
Chop the roasted chicken into bite-size pieces and stir it into your mixing pot with the roasted onion, the pan juices and the cooked rice.
Fold about half the green sauce through the whole batch and hold the rest back to spoon on at reheat time so it stays fresh and loud.

name: Peruvian Tallarines Verdes con Carne (Green Spaghetti with Beef)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Thaw and squeeze the frozen chopped spinach as dry as you can get it. Water is the enemy of this sauce.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the garlic gently until fragrant but not browned.
Blend the spinach, fresh basil, cooked garlic and its oil, walnuts, butter crackers, milk, ricotta cheese, and parmesan cheese until smooth and thick, then season with salt and black pepper.
Cook the rice according to the package to serve underneath.
Season the beef with salt and plenty of black pepper and sear it hard in a very hot pan, in batches, until browned outside and still pink within, then rest it and slice against the grain.
Warm the green sauce gently over low heat, stirring, and thin it with a splash of milk if it has tightened up. Do not boil it or the cheese will go grainy.
Taste and adjust the salt, since spinach and cheese sauces almost always need more than you expect.

name: Ground Beef Philly Cheesesteak Bowls
steps: Brown the ground beef in a big skillet, breaking it up as it cooks, then drain off any grease.
Add the sliced mushrooms, green peppers, and onion and cook until they soften, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic and a splash of beef broth, then let it simmer a couple minutes to pull it all together.
Kill the heat and lay the provolone over the top so it melts into the beef.
Spoon it over cooked white rice and stir once so every bite gets some cheese.

name: Picadinho de Carne (Brazilian Beef and Vegetable Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into a small dice, about half inch cubes, and pat it dry. Wet beef will not brown.
Sear the beef in the olive oil in batches over high heat, giving each batch room. Pull it out as it browns.
Cook the chopped onion and garlic in the same pot until soft, scraping up the browned bits.
Stir in the tomato paste and the cumin and cook a minute so the paste darkens.
Return the beef with the beef broth, cover, and simmer 60 to 75 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the diced carrots and sweet potatoes and simmer uncovered another 20 to 25 minutes, until they are soft and the stew has thickened.
Turn off the heat, stir in the red wine vinegar and the chopped cilantro, then taste for salt and pepper.

name: Polish Leczo (Kielbasa and Peppers Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the onions, cut the bell peppers into wide strips, slice the smoked sausage into coins and mince the garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot and cook the onions until they turn soft and translucent.
Add the sausage coins and brown them so the edges caramelize and leave color in the pot.
Add the pepper strips and cook until they slump and start to sweeten, which takes longer than you think it will.
Stir in the garlic, then pull the pot off the heat and add the sweet and smoked paprika so it does not scorch.
Back on the burner, stir in the tomato sauce and tomato paste, season with salt and black pepper, and simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens and turns glossy.
Cook the rice separately and keep it apart from the stew until you portion, so it does not turn to mush in the fridge.

name: Poppy Seed Chicken and Rice Casserole
ingredients: 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 14 oz (397 g)
Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 2.25 lb (1029 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 3.75 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Cube the chicken breast and cook it in a skillet with a spoonful of the butter over medium-high until it reaches 165 F. Set aside.
In your big pot, melt the rest of the butter, setting aside about 3 tablespoons of it for the topping, and cook the diced onion 4 minutes, then the garlic for 1 more.
Whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the chicken broth and heavy cream until smooth and simmering.
Drop in the cream cheese and stir until melted, then add the poppy seeds, salt, and pepper.
Fold in the chicken and the cooked rice, then spread into a greased 9x13 pan.
Crush the butter crackers, toss them with the reserved melted butter, scatter them over the top, and bake at 350 F for 20 to 25 minutes until the topping is golden and the edges bubble.

name: Pork Chops and Scalloped Potatoes Casserole
ingredients: Cream of Mushroom Soup (Campbell's (USDA SR)): 2.7 cans (818 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350F and butter a large deep baking dish.
Peel the potatoes and slice them thin and even, and slice the onion thin as well.
Whisk the cream of mushroom soup with the milk until it is smooth, and season it with salt and black pepper.
Layer half the potatoes and half the onion in the dish, pour over half the sauce, then repeat with the rest and dot the top with the butter.
Season the pork chops with salt and black pepper, brown them quickly in a hot skillet for color, and lay them on top of the potatoes.
Cover with foil and bake for about 75 minutes, then uncover for 20 minutes more until the potatoes are tender all the way through and the top has browned.

name: Pork Egg Roll in a Bowl
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice according to the package and set it aside to steam.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wide pot over medium-high heat.
Add the ground pork, break it apart, and cook until browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and diced yellow onion and cook until the onion softens.
Add the shredded cabbage and carrots and cook, stirring often, until the cabbage wilts down but still has some bite.
Pour in the soy sauce, toss everything together, and season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Combine the rice and the pork and cabbage mixture in your big pot, stir, and finish with the sliced green onions.

name: Pork Fried Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice a day ahead if you can, spread it on a sheet pan to cool, and refrigerate it uncovered.
Slice the pork tenderloin thin against the grain and season it with salt and black pepper.
Heat some of the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat and cook the pork in batches until just done, then set it aside.
Beat the eggs, scramble them in the same pan until barely set, and set them aside with the pork.
Add the rest of the oil and cook the diced onion, carrots, garlic, and ginger until the carrots soften.
Add the cold rice and the frozen peas and stir-fry hard, pressing the rice against the hot pan so it toasts rather than steams.
Return the pork and egg, pour in the soy sauce, toss everything together, then finish off the heat with the sesame oil and the sliced green onions.

name: Pork Ginger Carrot Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice according to the package and set it aside to steam.
Grate or julienne the carrots and grate the ginger, and slice the green onions, keeping the whites and greens separate.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the ginger, garlic, and green onion whites for about thirty seconds.
Add the ground pork, break it up, and cook until browned with no pink remaining.
Add the carrots and cook, stirring often, until they soften and start to sweeten.
Pour in the soy sauce and chicken broth and let it bubble down until the pan is glossy rather than wet.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and the green onion tops, and season with salt and black pepper.

name: Pork Milanese with Roasted Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425 F. Cube the potatoes, toss with a spoonful of the vegetable oil, salt, and pepper, and roast 30 to 35 minutes until browned, flipping once.
Slice the pork tenderloin into medallions, then pound each between plastic wrap to about a quarter inch thin.
Set up three dishes: flour with salt and pepper, eggs beaten with the milk, and the bread crumbs.
Dredge each cutlet flour, then egg wash, then crumbs, pressing so the coating sticks.
Pan-fry in batches in the hot vegetable oil, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and 145 F inside. Drain on a rack, not paper towels, so the crust stays crisp.
Salt the cutlets the second they leave the pan, and pack them alongside the roasted potatoes.

name: Pork Tenderloin Stroganoff over Egg Noodles
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 1 cups (210 g)
Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 28 oz dry (794 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the egg noodles in salted water until just al dente, drain, and set aside. They finish softening in the sauce, so do not overcook them here.

Cut the pork tenderloin into bite-size pieces and season with salt, black pepper, and the smoked paprika. Sear in batches in about half the butter over medium-high heat until they hit 145F, then move them to a plate.
Melt the rest of the butter in the same pot and cook the mushrooms and onions until browned and their liquid cooks off, about 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in the garlic for the last minute.

Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, and lemon juice. Simmer until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon, seasoning with the Italian seasoning as it goes.
Return the pork and any juices to the pot and warm through. Pull the pot off the heat, then stir in the light sour cream. Off the heat matters, boiling sour cream is how you get a grainy sauce.
Fold the noodles into the sauce until everything is coated and glossy.

name: Pozole Rojo (Red Pork and Hominy Stew) Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Stem and seed the dried guajillo and ancho chiles, toast them in a dry skillet about 30 seconds a side until they smell nutty, then soak them in hot water for 20 minutes.
Blend the softened chiles with some of their soaking water, several cloves of garlic, the chili powder, ground cumin, dried oregano and a spoon of cocoa powder into a smooth sauce, then strain it.
Cube the pork shoulder, season it with salt and black pepper, and brown it hard in the vegetable oil in your big pot, working in batches.
Fry the strained chile sauce in the pot for five minutes so it darkens and loses its raw edge, then return all the pork.
Pour in the chicken broth, add the dried arbol chiles whole if you want heat, and simmer covered for about 2 hours until the pork is fully tender.
Add the drained hominy and simmer 20 minutes more so it takes on the red broth, then cook the rice per the package to serve alongside.

name: Puerto Rican Pernil Pork Bowls with Rice and Beans
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 1.75 tbsp (26 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Mash the garlic with salt, dried oregano, ground cumin, onion powder, chili powder, black pepper and a little sugar into a paste, then loosen it with the olive oil, apple cider vinegar and lime juice.
Cut deep slits all over the pork shoulder and force the paste into every one of them, then rub whatever is left across the whole surface. Cover and refrigerate at least overnight.
Lay a bed of thick sliced onion in a roasting pan, set the pork on top fat side up, and roast covered at 300F for about 4 hours.
Uncover, raise the oven to 425F, and roast 20 to 30 minutes more until the outside is dark and crisp.
Rest the pork 20 minutes, then pull it apart with two forks and toss the meat through the pan juices and the softened onions.
Cook the rice per the package while the pork rests, so it is hot when you assemble.

name: Puerto Rican Pollo Guisado
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3215 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Season the chicken thighs with the sazon seasoning, dried oregano, salt and black pepper. Heat the vegetable oil in your largest pot over medium-high and brown them in batches until they have real color, then set them aside.
Cook the diced onion in the same pot for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and cook one more minute, scraping the fond up off the bottom.
Stir in the salsa and let it cook down for 3 to 4 minutes until it darkens and most of the water has left it. This is your sofrito step, and it needs the time.
Add the tomato sauce, bay leaves and chicken broth, then return the chicken with all its juices and bring the pot up to a simmer.
Cover and simmer 25 minutes, then add the cubed potato and sliced carrots and cook another 20 to 25 minutes uncovered, until the potatoes are tender and the broth has reduced into a proper gravy.
Stir in the olives during the last 5 minutes so they warm through without going rubbery.
Pull the bay leaves, break the chicken into large chunks with a spoon, and stir the whole pot so the potato starch thickens the gravy.

name: Pulled Pork Baked Mac and Cheese
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 11.75 oz (330 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 4.75 oz (132 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 4.75 oz (132 g)
Pasta Shells (Great Value): 24.75 oz dry (700 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Season the pork shoulder with salt, black pepper, ground cumin, dried oregano and dried thyme, sear it in the olive oil, then slow cook it with the diced onion, minced jalapeno, garlic and orange juice until it shreds.
Boil the pasta shells in salted water until just under al dente. They will finish in the oven, so pulling them early is the difference between good and mushy.
Melt the butter in a large pot, whisk in the flour, and cook it two minutes until it smells nutty but has not colored.
Pour in the heavy cream slowly while whisking, bring it to a bare simmer, then add the Dijon mustard and take it off the heat.
Stir in the shredded cheddar, mozzarella and Mexican cheese blend a handful at a time until the sauce is smooth, then fold in the drained pasta.
Spread half the mac in a large baking dish, layer the pulled pork across it, top with the rest of the mac, and bake at 375F for 25 minutes, then broil briefly for a browned top.

name: Pulled Pork Enchilada Bake
ingredients: Enchilada Sauce (Old El Paso): 3.5 cans (990 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 28 oz (794 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 3.5 cans (892 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (844 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slow cook the pork shoulder with salt, black pepper, ground cumin and chili powder until it shreds, then pull it and drain off the excess liquid.
Cook the diced onion and chopped green bell peppers in the olive oil until soft, then add the minced garlic for the last minute.
Toss the pulled pork with the cooked vegetables, the barbecue sauce and about half the enchilada sauce until everything is coated.

Spread a thin layer of the remaining enchilada sauce in a large baking pan, then layer tortillas, pork mixture, drained black beans, drained corn and shredded cheddar. Repeat the layers until the pan is full.
Finish with tortillas, the last of the enchilada sauce and a heavy layer of cheddar on top.
Bake at 375F for 30 to 35 minutes until it bubbles at the edges, then let it rest 15 minutes before cutting so the layers set.

name: Pulled Pork Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 10.25 oz (289 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the pork shoulder with salt, black pepper and Italian seasoning, sear it in the olive oil, then slow cook it until it shreds and pull it apart.
Boil the peeled and quartered potatoes in salted water until they fall off a knife, then drain them well and let the steam escape for a minute.
Mash the potatoes with the butter and heavy cream, season with salt and black pepper, and stop as soon as they are smooth. Overworked potatoes turn gluey.
Cook the diced onion and sliced carrots in a skillet until soft, add the minced garlic, then sprinkle the flour over and stir for two minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes, the beef broth, the balsamic vinegar and the Worcestershire sauce and simmer until it thickens into a gravy, then fold in the pulled pork, the frozen peas and the corn.
Spread the filling in a large baking dish, spoon the mashed potatoes over the top and rake ridges into them with a fork, then bake at 400F for 30 minutes until browned and bubbling.

name: Pulled Pork Tamale Pie with Cornbread Topping
ingredients: Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 1.6 cans (185 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 6.5 oz (185 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the pork loin with salt, chili powder, garlic powder, ground cumin, dried oregano, paprika and black pepper, sear it in the vegetable oil, then slow cook it until it shreds easily.
Shred the pork, drain most of the liquid, and stir in the canned diced green chiles.
Spread the pork and chile mixture across the bottom of a large greased baking dish and scatter about half the shredded cheddar over it.
Whisk the grits, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt together in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the eggs with the heavy cream, the melted butter and the sour cream, then stir the wet into the dry just until it comes together. Do not overmix or the topping goes tough.
Pour the batter over the pork, spread it to the edges, top with the remaining cheddar, and bake at 375F for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden and set.

name: Red Beans, Turkey Sausage and Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground turkey in your largest pot over medium-high heat, breaking it into coarse crumbles and letting it get real color before you stir it.
Season the turkey heavily with dried thyme, salt, and black pepper while it browns, so it reads like sausage rather than plain ground meat.
Add the diced onion, green bell pepper, and celery and cook 8 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic for one more minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and let it cook against the bottom of the pot for two minutes until it darkens, which takes the raw edge off it.
Add the canned diced tomatoes, the drained kidney beans, and the hot sauce, then simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes, mashing some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy.
Cook the rice separately while the beans simmer, so the grains stay distinct instead of dissolving into the sauce.
Taste for salt and heat, then serve the beans over the rice or fold them together for portioning.

name: Ropa Vieja Rice Bowls
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 1.75 tbsp (26 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the steak with salt, black pepper, cumin, oregano, and turmeric and lay it in the slow cooker.
Slice the onion and green bell peppers into strips and scatter them over the beef with the minced garlic.
Stir the tomato paste into the beef broth until smooth, then pour it over along with the diced tomatoes and their juice.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef pulls into strands with almost no effort.
Shred the beef directly in the cooker with two forks and stir it back through the peppers and sauce.
Stir in the sliced olives and the apple cider vinegar and let it sit 10 minutes on the heat so the flavors settle.
Cook the rice separately and taste the sauce for salt, remembering the olives brought plenty.

name: Salisbury Steak and Potato Bowls
ingredients: Worcestershire Sauce (Lea & Perrins): 1 tsp (patties) + 1/2 tsp (gravy) (25 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Mix the ground beef with the bread crumbs and shape into patties.
Brown the patties in a large skillet, then set them aside.
Cook the sliced mushrooms and onions in the same pan until soft.
Stir in the beef broth and tomato paste and let it simmer into a gravy, then return the patties to the pan.
Roast or boil the potatoes until fork tender.
Serve the patties and gravy over the potatoes.

name: Sausage, Cabbage and Apple Skillet
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 3.5 tbsp (52 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins, slice the onion, core and shred the cabbage, and core and slice the apples thick.
Heat the olive oil in your largest skillet and brown the sausage coins hard on both sides, then set them aside.
Cook the sliced onion in the sausage fat until it softens and picks up the color from the pan.
Add the cabbage in batches, letting each handful wilt before the next goes in, and cook until it turns tender and sweet.
Add the apple slices and cook just a few minutes. You want them softened but still holding their shape, not collapsed.
Whisk the chicken broth, apple juice, dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar and dried thyme together, pour it into the skillet, and simmer until it reduces and glazes everything.
Return the sausage, season with salt and black pepper, and cook the rice separately to serve underneath.

name: Sausage Hash Brown and Egg Casserole
ingredients: Frozen Hash Browns (Great Value): 18.25 cups (1538 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350F and grease two large baking dishes.

Brown the ground pork in a skillet, breaking it into crumbles, seasoning as it cooks with the salt, black pepper, garlic powder and onion powder. Drain off the excess fat or the casserole will come out greasy.
Spread the frozen hash browns across the bottoms of the baking dishes. There is no need to thaw them first.
Scatter the cooked sausage over the potatoes, then most of the shredded cheddar over that.
Whisk the eggs and milk together with a little more salt and pepper until it is completely uniform, then pour it evenly over both dishes.
Top with the rest of the cheddar and bake until the center is set and no longer jiggles when you nudge the pan.
Let it rest at least ten minutes before you cut it. Cutting a hot casserole gets you a puddle instead of a square.

name: Scalloped Potato Turkey Casserole
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 8.25 oz (237 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the potatoes about an eighth of an inch thick, skins on or off as you prefer, and keep them in cold water until you are ready so they do not brown.
Whisk the milk, eggs, flour, Dijon mustard, salt, and plenty of black pepper together until completely smooth. This is the custard that holds the whole thing together.
Melt the butter with the garlic and stir it into the custard, which distributes the fat and garlic evenly instead of leaving pockets.
Drain and dry the potato slices, then layer a third of them into a greased and buttered 9x13 pan, followed by a third of the diced turkey breast and a scatter of cheddar.
Repeat the layers twice more, then pour the custard slowly over the top and press the whole thing down so the liquid works into every layer.
Cover with foil and bake at 375F for 50 minutes, then uncover, add the last of the cheddar, and bake 20 to 25 minutes more until the top is browned and a knife slides through with no resistance.
Rest 20 minutes before portioning. Scalloped potatoes need that time to firm up or they will slide apart on the spatula.

name: Senegalese Chicken Mafe (Peanut Stew)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.25 lb (1890 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Season the chicken thighs with salt, black pepper and smoked paprika. Heat the vegetable oil in your largest pot over medium-high and brown the chicken in batches, working in a single layer so it colors instead of steams. Set it aside.
Drop the diced onion into the same pot and cook 5 to 6 minutes until soft and starting to catch, then add the garlic and the minced jalapeno and cook one more minute.
Stir the peanut butter directly into the hot onions and let it toast for a minute. It will look wrong and seize up. That is exactly what it should do.
Add the diced tomatoes and the chicken broth a little at a time, whisking as you go so the peanut butter loosens into a smooth sauce instead of clumping.

Return the chicken and any juices to the pot, bring it to a simmer, then cover and hold it at a low bubble for 45 minutes to an hour, stirring now and then so the bottom does not scorch. Peanut butter sauces catch fast.
While it simmers, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Pull the chicken, shred or chop it, and stir it back into the sauce with the cooked rice folded through so every bowl gets both.

name: Senegalese Chicken Yassa (Lemon Onion Chicken)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.5 lb (2917 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Toss the chicken thighs with the lemon juice, half the sliced onion, the minced garlic, grated ginger, black pepper and salt. Let that sit in the fridge for at least an hour, or overnight if you plan ahead.
Lift the chicken out and shake off the onion. Heat the vegetable oil in your largest pot over medium-high and brown the thighs in batches until they have real color, then set them aside.

Dump every bit of the onion, the marinade included, into the pot. Turn the heat to medium and let them cook down for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they collapse into a soft golden jam. This step is the recipe. Do not rush it.
Stir in the dijon mustard, the minced jalapeno and the bay leaves, then pour in the chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the pot clean.
Return the chicken and its juices, cover, and simmer 30 to 35 minutes until the thighs are tender and read 165F.
While it simmers, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Pull the bay leaves, stir in the olives, chop the chicken into bite-size pieces, and fold the cooked rice through the pot so every serving gets sauce and grain together.

name: Senfbraten (German Mustard-Gravy Pork Roast)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the pork loin dry, season it with salt and black pepper, and coat the whole surface in a thick layer of the dijon mustard. Hold a couple of spoonfuls back for the gravy.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot or roasting pan and sear the mustard coated loin on all sides until it browns.
Take the roast out and cook the sliced onions, the garlic and the sliced carrots in the same pot until they soften and pick up the fond.
Pour in the beef broth and chicken broth, add the bay leaves and dried thyme, and scrape the bottom of the pot clean.
Set the roast back in, cover, and braise low until the center reaches 145F and the meat slices easy.
Move the roast to a board to rest. Reduce the braising liquid on the stovetop, whisk in the butter and the reserved mustard, and taste it for salt.
Slice the rested pork thin against the grain, cook the rice separately, and combine everything with the gravy in your big pot.

name: Sheet-Pan BBQ Turkey Meatballs over Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the ground turkey with the eggs, bread crumbs, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper using your hands, stopping the moment it comes together.
Roll the mixture into golf-ball sized meatballs and arrange them on two oiled sheet pans with space between each one. Crowded meatballs steam instead of browning.
Scatter the drained pineapple chunks, the onion wedges, and the red bell pepper pieces around the meatballs, then drizzle everything with the vegetable oil.
Roast at 425F for 20 minutes, until the meatballs are browned and the pineapple edges start to caramelize.
Brush the meatballs and the vegetables generously with the barbecue sauce and return the pans for 8 to 10 minutes so the glaze tightens and the centers reach 165F.
Cook the rice while the pans are in the oven, so everything comes together hot at the same time.
Spoon the meatballs, pineapple, and peppers over the rice and finish with the sliced green onions.
